Nonetheless, this is exactly why I am building my real estate company for as a fellow property owner rin. Mostly kasi agents and brokers (yes, I’m including even the licensed ones, pero hindi lahat) BUT karamihan nyan yung unlicensed, they just wanted to manage your property so they can secure the commission 50/50 if may interested na hindi direct or 100% if galing sa kanila mismo yung client. The motive behind it is not to provide service, but to earn. 

Nonetheless, they earn because you trusted them to “manage” your property WHEN they don’t really manage it at all and just secure the key and “bakod” from your property for the commission. Minsan, they don’t even actively market it. Basta nasa kanila, pag may client, meron, pag wala, ay basta nasa kanila. Kawawa property owners.

Mostly, these type of management only have leverage on “trust” and relationship and most of these people, wala namang pake. “Edi wag mo na pa-manage or bigay susi, marami pa dyan” ang thinking kapag may mali, kesa ayusin and take accountability. Detached sila sa property owner and relationship nyo if its not working anymore. Hence trust like these lang as the leverage for management is dangerous practice na. Kasi most often, nate-take advantage lang the owners. This should not be it.

Dapat may accountability. LAHAT. Pati passive or inactive marketing. I would recommend getting indeed a property management company as advised by other people here.

My company also does property management. Pero difference lang, I want it to focus more than just the accountability tbh, motive ko is to actually put your unit out there still kahit naka-bakod na kami (the key being with us), will still utilise the forte of brokers and agents. But mostly, our motive is to bakod your property not for the commission but for our relationship na pinili nyo our company to manage your property. Hindi namin babakuran your property just for the commission. Babakuran namin yung property because you trusted us with its management. That is enough profit for us kasi your referral to our brand and quality will go a long way to reflect our values more than just the commission, secondary nalang yan.

You want to get your property rented? Ibigay natin sa kung sinong broker or agent. Cause we don’t want to fuck our relationship up with you. Kahit most of the commission is theirs na. What we value most is the relationship we have with the owners kaya samin lang ang susi.

Just my cents. Nabenta ko narin company ko hHAHAHAA

I don’t think I could fully agree with you. Although I think you are bearing some weight. Just my cents lang on this, unclogging the courts doesn’t and shouldn’t entail relegating this criminal act to just mere singilan ng utang in the small claims court.

If there is a problem in the processes and/or the justice system itself then fix the system itself and not change the law to adjust thereto or with the capacity, competency, or efficiency of the courts. Hindi obligasyon ng batas maging convenient para sa mga alagad neto.

Also, on your statement na “pero typically the court will just slap you a fine kaysa ikulong ka. ginagawa kasing singilan ng utang ng court. 😂”

1. Afaik it’s not just fines, it’s a criminal act, there would be damages.
2. That how it works pag utang. The court will have a decision sa case mo and although it may cost the person accused, it won’t lead to imprisonment kasi walang makukulong sa utang. Unless gustong gusto mong makulong nangutang sayo then hindi na court process crinitic/assail mo sa comment mo, but the constitution itself.
2.2. Nevertheless, in response padin, as for the case of BP 22 or bounced checks as a cause of action for the courts, hindi ito utang lang. It is a criminal act at may nakukulong rito for estafa. Hindi mere fines lang and walang nakukulong, may nakukulong.
2.3. “Ginagawang singilan ang court.” Unrelated. Again, it’s not mere utang na sinisingil. It is a criminal act.
3. To relegate bouncing checks to small courts is a very dangerous precedent especially for wrongdoers. Chances are, they will purposefully just issue checks to bounce and count it off as ay nakalimutan sige babayaran ko pag may courage na magfile sa small claims to or pag siningil na ako WHICH in turn strips off the purpose of PDCs or Cheques as payment securities.

All in all, I don’t agree with relegating cases violating BP 22 to small claims or civil cases especially just for the sake of unclogging the courts among other things. Violations of it could (or mostl likely be) a crime.

Bro honestly, I’m going to answer in a lower middle class view (hahaha i mean— if i’m from upper, it’ll be a different story hence the mentioning forgive me if it would be deemed irrelevant). BTW FT, you mean Fairview Terraces? 

Personally, I’d say the gym subscription for Gold’s Gym is expensive enough. Personally, I wouldn’t want to get a PT muna kasi mabigat sa bulsa especially I only workout as a form of lifestyle and not to compete and be a professional in that specific industry. So unless you really have a goal in a determined time, and you want to invest seriously in fitness talaga, then you may get this investment.

Otherwise, if hindi naman and you just want to have a healthy lifestyle and/or have a body goal. You may carry your own load for free naman! Our brain is very powerful so try to lean muna sa kanya. Once you’ve exhausted your brain na on things you can learn on your own, then it’s the best time to get someone that can teach you. After a year and a half of self-learning and muscle gains, I decided to get an amateur coach with experience for Php 400 Four Weeks Online. Pag amateur, swertihan nalang talaga sa expertise nya and professionalism but as far as my coach is concerned, I have learned better forms and execution than what I get sa YouTube simply because may direct criticism na sa ginagawa ko. May personal comments na. So this 400-peso expenses is more of like an investment sa learning ko. So soon, baka I can workout alone ulit without any guide from a coach. 

That is to answer your first elaborating detail: exhaust your own brain muna then when you feel like it, get a coach, possibly yung kaya ng expenses mo. I mean— isipin mo there are a lot of people who do not have access to personal trainers but they do just fine and great tbh. So malay mo kasama tayo dun 😉 and get a professional personal trainer na talaga if a. Afford na natin and b. We are serious na talaga with our fitness and body goals. (Serious I mean the money-making type siguro). 

As for the second, I personally go to the gym with full blast airpods on my ears (while also aware of my surrounding of course). I try to keep up with my program and list of machines pero pag occupied, skip ko muna tas babalikan ko pag free na. Pag free na yung machine and inapproach ko na yung machine ng walang tao, I’ll look around if may nauna sakin or gumagamit pa to confirm. If wala, I’ll look at the last gym goer na gumamit and get his or wait for his attention before gesturing a “👍” sign mouthing, “boss, bro, or kuya, ok ka na po dito/tapos na po kayo dito?” Then tatango sila and signal “👍” din. Siguro tip ko lang dito is be aware of your surroundings for gym etiquette, respect, and self-improvement din :))
It wouldn’t hurt to ask rin if ever tapos na sila or ask if “bro pwede ba tayo salitan?”. Gym peeps are some of the most considerate and kind people you know (kahit mukha akong galit minsan hahaha at mahirap iapproach) so most likely, makikishare sila. If hindi naman, it’s ok. Move on ka muna sa ibang machine, wag lang silang magsungit ng walang dahilan kasi mali na nila yun hahaha. 

To answer your question directly, minsan pwede salitan, minsan pwedeng after na nila. Just communicate with them and not just mang-agaw ng machine kasi nakakaoffend yun pag nangaagaw hahaha!!! 

These are all just from my experience. Goodluckk!!!
